text:
Predicates:
Occurs(x, y) ::: x occurs in y.
Get(x, y) ::: x gets y.
Monkeypox(x) ::: x is Monkeypox.
Virus(x) ::: x is a virus.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Human(x) ::: x is a human.
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Fever(x) ::: x has a fever.
Headache(x) ::: x has a headache.
MusclePains(x) ::: x has muscle pains.
Tiredness(x) ::: x has tiredness.
Flu(x) ::: x is the flu.
Premises:
∀x ∀y ((Virus(x) ∧ Monkeypox(x) ∧ Occurs(x, y)) → Get(y, Monkeypox(x))) ::: When the Monkeypox virus occurs in a being, it may get Monkeypox.
∃x ∃y (Virus(x) ∧ Monkeypox(x) ∧ Animal(y) ∧ Occurs(x, y)) ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals.
∀x (Human(x) → Mammal(x)) ::: Humans are mammals.
∀x (Mammal(x) → Animal(x)) ::: Mammals are animals.
∀x (Get(x, Monkeypox(x)) → (Fever(x) ∧ Headache(x) ∧ MusclePains(x) ∧ Tiredness(x))) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include fever, headache, muscle pains, and tiredness.
∀x (Flu(x) → Tiredness(x)) ::: People feel tired when they get the flu.
Conclusion:
¬∃x Flu(x) ::: No one gets the flu.
